# Seeds whose SELF-HOST x86-64 result disagrees with the interpreter's, for
# TestDifferential_SelfHostX86_64 (internal/e2e/diff_oracle_selfhost_test.go).
#
# Format: <seed> <reason + issue>. Blank lines and # comments ignored.
#
# A row is a KNOWN COMPILER BUG being tolerated so the rest of the corpus keeps
# running — not a seed that is allowed to be wrong. The leg fails on a NEW
# divergence and equally on a LISTED seed that starts agreeing, so this list
# prunes itself as the bugs are fixed rather than becoming somewhere they are
# forgotten.
#
# For every row here the interpreter, native x86-64 and native arm64 agree with
# each other; that agreement is what says the self-host compiler is wrong rather
# than the generated program being invalid.
#
# THE LIST IS EMPTY. Every seed the leg can compile now agrees with the
# interpreter. Keep the file — an empty list is the strongest form of the gate,
# since any divergence at all fails the leg — and keep the record below of what
# left, because it is what the next round of probing should be measured against.
#
# Measured 2026-08-06 over seeds 0..511 (the leg's default corpus), after #6283
# and the fail_why work: 361 agree, 0 diverge, 151 compile gaps. Count the gaps,
# not just the agreements, when reading a run: the leg only proves what it could
# COMPILE, so a fix that turns a wrong answer into an IR bail raises the gap
# count while looking like a win in the divergence column.
#
# That caution cuts both ways, and the last seven runs went the other way: 204
# agree / 308 gaps, then 263 / 249 (#6237 + #6246), 291 / 221 (#6261), 311 / 201
# (#6268), 325 / 187 (#6272), 338 / 174 (#6276), 361 / 151. One bail can cost far
# more than the seed that exposes it — an if-expression whose branches are 64-bit
# took the whole MODULE off the IR path, and fernsmith emits if-expressions
# everywhere, so a single missing branch in one classifier was suppressing a
# tenth of the corpus.
#
# HOW TO READ A BAIL: just run it. `FERN_STRICT_IR=1` now names the innermost AST
# node that refused, via LowerState.fail_why —
#
#   FERN_STRICT_IR: gen_f0 (did not lower: `return` of binary `|`)
#
# This replaces a gdb recipe that used to live here (build with -g, break on
# LowerState.fail, read the caller's line). That recipe worked and is how the
# census below was first built, but it is now strictly worse than reading the
# message, so it has been deleted rather than left as a second way to do the
# same thing.
#
# CENSUS OF THE 151 GAPS, so the next round is aimed rather than sampled:
#
#   90  function value <fn>$clo not defined   → #6256, and now more than half the
#                                               pile on its own. NOT one
#                                               mechanism — the issue's own
#                                               comments record that correction:
#                                               several shapes share this
#                                               message, and grouping by message
#                                               is what made the first reduction
#                                               fix the wrong thing. It has grown
#                                               71 → 78 → 90 while nothing about
#                                               it changed, purely because seeds
#                                               that used to stop earlier now
#                                               reach it. Read a moved number as
#                                               a reordering before a regression.
#   14  call to unknown symbol T.to_string    → a method call on a bare type var.
#   47  a named fail_why, grouped by shape:
#         13  `return` of a BINARY op (| * % >> << / -| *|)
#          9  `return` of an IDENT (mostly `__chk_v0`, a %?/ /? match binding)
#          9  `return` of a CALL (`id`, `pick` — the erased generics)
#          9  an immediately-invoked value block (if/match-expression or
#             comprehension desugar), incl. 2 in `return` and 1 in an assignment
#          4  tuple literal / array literal / field access
#          3  other
#
# The 47 are what to reduce next: each names its own shape, so they need no
# instrumentation, and the `return`-of-X rows are 31 of them. Whether they share
# a cause is UNMEASURED — the $clo pile is the standing warning against assuming
# a shared message means a shared mechanism, and these share a shape, not even a
# message. Re-measure before picking: draining one pile reshuffles the others.

# CRASHES — the self-host-compiled binary died by SIGSEGV where the interpreter
# returned a value. These were ONE bug: #6207, a `Map { … }` literal whose keys
# the parser could not classify, building itself string-keyed so map_set
# compared integer keys through __fern_str_eq. Eight rows left with it —
# 200 / 228 / 455 with the two classifiable key forms (#6213 leaf-reachable
# arithmetic, #6220 cast targets), then 59 / 97 / 144 once the fix stopped being
# syntactic and read the `Map[K, V]` declaration instead. Every crash row in the
# corpus was that bug; the header used to hedge that the survivors might be "a
# different cause (or causes)", which was true of what had been measured at the
# time and false once they were reduced.

# WRONG VALUES + ARENA EXHAUSTION — both sections emptied together, because they
# were ONE bug. infer_expr_width classified a number literal by MAGNITUDE alone,
# so a small suffixed literal (`7i64`) read as 32 bits and every 64-bit value
# derived from one was computed at the wrong width. Fifteen rows left with that
# fix: 4, 20, 28, 29, 48, 52, 99, 117, 123, 241, 324, 362, 364, 375, 482. The
# old note here — that the interp=0 rows were "worth checking as a group before
# reducing them one at a time" — was right; 117's "arena exhausted" was a
# symptom of the same mis-widening, not a separate leak.
#
# Seed 502 left in two steps. #6228 first moved it from a silent wrong answer to
# an IR bail (`FERN_STRICT_IR: __lam_22`) — the safe direction, but a gap rather
# than a fix — and #6237 then closed the bail, so it now compiles and agrees.
#
# The cause was NOT irt_guess, which this note used to name and which cost an
# hour to rule out. A lifted if-EXPRESSION gets its return type from
# `if_expr_rt` at PARSE time, and because that writes a non-EMPTY "i32",
# infer_ret_types_module never revisits it — so irt_guess never runs on these
# lambdas at all. Teaching irt_guess the suffix AND the magnitude changes
# nothing; measured, twice. `if_expr_rt` was the fourth literal classifier in
# parser.fern and the last one that read neither.
#
# The hole PREDATED the width work either way: a big-magnitude branch
# (`if (c) { 5000000000 } else { … }`) bailed identically before #6228, with no
# suffix involved.

# Also gone earlier, with their own fixes: 121 / 265 / 365 (#6177, the maps
# runtime need-gate).
